verdict.rationale: Base44 documents its own per-app sandbox that external AI coding agents or scripts can connect to. It also documents an eject/clone command that creates a separate project with its own app ID, which could serve as an isolated copy. However, no evidence says the sandbox isolates test data from the live app's production data, and the testing agent is not described as running against a separate environment. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that sandbox/test runs use non-production data, a documented staging or test environment separate from production, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Bring your own AI coding agent, or your own scripts, to a Base44 app by connecting to its sandbox.
Clone an existing Base44 app into a separate local project. This command downloads the frontend code and backend resources from a selected app and creates a new project with its own app ID.
The testing agent runs browser-based tests on your app's key flows, simulating real user interactions like submitting a form, completing a checkout, or navigating between pages.
